answer: Lantern-island lease auctions: each agent's visible identity slot leases a unique "lantern" on an "island" (shard) whose renewal price scales with the inverse of island occupancy variance, and cross-island routing requires an "orchard" graft fee proportional to the square of new links added. Attacker cost grows superlinearly: saturating k islands to look organic raises per-slot renewal fees on sparse islands and makes each forged graft pay quadratic linking costs, so marginal sybil cost exceeds marginal yield before majority share.
